title: Rigveda 9.56: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.56: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.56 is a hymn of 4 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 687v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.56.1-4 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 1, varga 13); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 687v
translation.original_text:
1pari̱ soma̍ ṛ̱tam bṛ̱had ā̱śuḥ pa̱vitre̍ arṣati | vi̱ghnan rakṣā̍ṁsi deva̱yuḥ ||
2yat somo̱ vāja̱m arṣa̍ti śa̱taṁ dhārā̍ apa̱syuva̍ḥ | indra̍sya sa̱khyam ā̍vi̱śan ||
3a̱bhi tvā̱ yoṣa̍ṇo̱ daśa̍ jā̱raṁ na ka̱nyā̍nūṣata | mṛ̱jyase̍ soma sā̱taye̍ ||
4tvam indrā̍ya̱ viṣṇa̍ve svā̱dur i̍ndo̱ pari̍ srava | nṝn sto̱tṝn pā̱hy aṁha̍saḥ ||
translation.text:
1SWIFT to the purifying sieve flows Soma as exalted Law, Slaying the fiends, loving the Gods.
2When Soma pours the strengthening food a hundred ever-active streams To Indra's friendship win theirway.
3Ten Dames have sung to welcome thee, even as a maiden greets her love: O Soma, thou art decked to win.
4Flow hitherward, O Indu, sweet to Indra and to Vishṇu: guard The men, the singers, from distress.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 687v (numbered 4v by the scribe) (OPenn image 688, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.54.4 ‹iti indra-yuḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 688r (numbered 5r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.57.2 ‹cakṣāṇaḥ arṣati hariḥ tuñjānaḥ›. Verses 9.56.1-4 end on this page.
